one_month_reasoning: CoreWeave's Q3-26 report is expected Nov 5-16 (not yet scheduled), so it most likely falls outside the Oct 31 window. Events inside the window: late-October hyperscaler earnings (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta), whose 2027 capex commentary (consensus heading to ~$1T) moves the neocloud group; follow-through on Meta Enterprise Platform, confirmed Sep 29, which sells compute externally and so is a negative for pricing power; and ongoing supply from the 35M-share ATM plus convert hedging after the Sep 18 $3.7B 2033 notes (conversion price $97.85), which caps rallies. The demand read from Nvidia (Aug 26) and Oracle (Sep 10) was strong and is already priced. I see no edge, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred just under spot ($88) at monthly vol 0.93/sqrt(12) ~ 27%, with a slight tilt down for ATM supply.

fair_value.method: Blend of DCF $54 (40%), 6.0x NTM EV/EBITDA $96 (35%) and 3.0x NTM EV/sales $69 (25%) = ~$72. The DCF (WACC 11.5%, capex 1.8x incremental revenue, 6.5-yr asset life, 55% terminal EBITDA margin, g 3%) shows that value hinges almost entirely on capital intensity and asset life.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF 2026Q4-2033 + Gordon terminal. Revenue $26.3B (2027) -> $40B/$52B/$60B/$66B/$70B/$72B (2033), g=3%; EBITDA margin 59% fading to 55%; capex = 1.8x incremental revenue run-rate + replacement of cohorts after 6 yrs (legacy $19B run-rate fleet replaced 2029-32); D&A life 6.5y; tax 21% from 2029 (NOLs before); WACC 11.5%; net debt ~$37.1B at Sep-26 (operating leases excluded because rent is already in adjusted EBITDA); 606M shares. EV $66B -> equity $28.6B = $47/sh today, rolled 12m at cost of equity 14.6% = $54. Sensitivity is extreme: capex intensity 1.6x/7y life gives ~$140; 2.0x/6y gives ~$0.

Q2-26 adj. EBITDA margin 59%; consensus 2027 EBITDA $15.6B/$26.3B = 59%. Fade by 4 pts for GPU rental deflation (H100 index ~$2.71/hr vs ~$8 peak) and Meta entering as a seller.

Reported: Jun-26 in-service gross PP&E $40.7B vs Q2 annualized revenue $10.3B (~3-4x legacy). New: GB300 rack $3-6.5M/72 GPUs (~$60-70k/GPU all-in) vs 6-yr fixed ~$4.00/GPU-hr (~$33k/yr) = ~2.0x; Q3 short-dated contracts at ~$40M/MW imply ~1.2x. Blended 1.8x.

10-yr UST close Sep 30, 2026.
Damodaran implied US ERP, Jan 2026.
Debt/equity ~8.9x (book) and the stock's 93% realized vol imply a high levered beta; 2.2 = ~0.4 correlation x 93%/17% market vol.
Effective rates on 2030-2032 senior notes 9-10% (10-Q debt table); 2033 converts at 2.875% are cheap but carry equity optionality, so excluded from marginal cost.

Jun-26 debt $35.07B (recourse $31.4B + non-recourse $3.66B) + finance leases $0.22B - cash $5.52B = $29.8B; + est. Q3 burn ~$8.3B (capex ~$9.5B less EBITDA/interest) - $1B Jane Street equity; $3.7B convert is debt-for-cash neutral.

bear.story: Compute scarcity eases in 2027 as CoWoS supply loosens, Meta/hyperscalers sell spare capacity, and H100/B200 rental indices keep deflating. Short-dated $40M/MW contracts reprice down at renewal, capex intensity stays near 2-3x, net debt passes $60B at ~10% marginal cost, and ATM/convert dilution continues. The market values the equity near the DCF low cases.

base.story: 2026 lands at about $12.8B revenue and the 2027 consensus (~$26B revenue, ~$15.6B EBITDA) is met. Backlog converts as power comes online (4.2 GW contracted), but GAAP losses, interest of $3B+/yr and dilution keep the multiple at ~5-6x EBITDA. The stock ends roughly flat.

bull.story: Scarcity persists through 2027 (Nvidia allocation sold out, hyperscaler capex ~$1T). New and renewed contracts at ~$40M/MW lift returns, so capex intensity trends toward 1.5x, the move to an investment-grade credit profile cuts funding costs, and the multiple re-rates toward the peer median (~6x sales).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$45 (about half the current price, roughly the equity value in my DCF at 2.0x capex intensity), the market would be pricing an impaired backlog, contracts repricing down at renewal, or refinancing stress on ~$40B+ of 9-11% debt. That would point to the unit economics failing, not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Industry evidence is mostly positive on demand and pricing. Nvidia's AI Clouds/Industrial/Enterprise data-center revenue grew 138% y/y to $40.3B with a $108B next-quarter guide. Oracle OCI grew 121% with RPO of $664B. Nebius ARR rose 56% q/q to $3.0B, and new neocloud deals are pricing at ~$20-40B per GW, roughly double a year ago. CoreWeave itself says Q3 contracts were signed at ~$40M/MW, consistent with the Ornn B200 index at ~$8/GPU-hr. Hyperscaler capex is heading to ~$1T in 2027 (a thin Manifold market leaned >$800B before resolving N/A). The negatives are also in the chain: older-GPU rental prices keep deflating (H100 ~$2.7-3.8/hr), Meta confirmed on Sep 29 it will sell compute externally, CoreWeave's revenue is concentrated (top two customers 62%), and its balance sheet is far more levered than Nebius's, with fresh ATM and convert issuance. Valuation: the cohort DCF shows that at today's reported economics (59% EBITDA margin but only a 5% adjusted operating margin, because D&A eats ~54% of revenue) equity value is very sensitive to capex intensity. My base (1.8x, 6.5 yrs, WACC 11.5%) gives $54. Multiples on NTM Oct-27 numbers, after ~$62B projected net debt, give $96 (6x EBITDA) and $69 (3x sales). The blend is ~$72, about 18% below the $88.57 spot; I put the distribution median (~$82) between fair value and spot because industry demand and pricing momentum are strong and a 12-month price need not converge to fair value. Analyst targets average $141.58 (41 analysts); I treat that as evidence of sell-side optimism, not as the answer. Distribution: lognormal, median ~$82, sigma ~0.72 (below the 93% realized vol but well above large-cap norms), with a slightly fatter left tail for leverage and distress (P(<$22) ~6%). Scenarios: 30% at $40 / 45% at $85 / 25% at $160, mean ~$90. Research was limited where Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage were plan- or rate-limited and DCD returned 403; X/Twitter was not attempted.
